plugins.name: autoresearch
plugins.tagline: Eval-driven improvement, plus the harness to drive it
plugins.summary: Two parts form one loop. An edit → eval → keep/discard engine improves code, prompts, or docs. It scores each change with a shell command, an LLM judge, or both. It shows progress in a live Artifact dashboard. A harness builder measures project health in six categories. It creates feedback loops, evals, sensors, and context management advisories. It then fixes the top-ranked issue through the same loop.
plugins.oneLiner: Eval-driven improvement loop (keep/discard with a live Artifact dashboard) plus a dev-lifecycle harness builder that measures project health and creates feedback loops, evals, and sensors. Inspired by karpathy/autoresearch.

commands.name: /autoresearch:harness-build
commands.description: Menu-driven scaffolder for harness components: feedback loop, eval loop, sensor, or context-mgmt advisory. Writes Tier-1 artifacts into your project's .claude/.

commands.name: /autoresearch:harness-check
commands.description: Scan project health across code quality, tests, runtime, architecture, scriptability, and harness completeness. Produces a scored harness report with impact-ranked improvements

commands.name: /autoresearch:harness-improvement
commands.description: Execute improvement loop on the top-ranked harness issue: auto-generates eval from probes and spawns the autoresearch:experimenter agent

commands.name: /autoresearch:improve
commands.description: Iteratively improve any artifact using an edit-eval-keep/discard loop with live dashboard

skills.name: experiment-loop
skills.description: Core iteration logic for autoresearch: edit target, run eval, keep or discard, update dashboard, repeat.

skills.name: harness-probes
skills.description: Guide for adding custom probes to the harness check system.

plugins.name: adhd-review
plugins.summary: One ruleset, three layers. Layer 1 shapes every reply — lead with the action, number multi-step work with time estimates, cut preamble/recap/closers, state errors matter-of-factly. Layer 2 governs the final turn of substantial multi-step work with Review-Ready buckets — ✅ Done / ⚠️ Broken / 🙋 What I need from you / 🤖 What I'll do, blockers before FYI, each ask naming why it's yours. A Visual Layer draws non-linear flow-shaped concepts — branches, loops, state changes, hierarchies — as fenced ASCII diagrams instead of prose, while linear steps stay numbered lists. Applies to the human-facing thread only: a default-on SessionStart hook injects the rules into the main session, so subagent returns stay full-detail. On by default — installing the plugin shapes the main thread out of the box; set CLAUDE_ADHD_REVIEW=0 to silence a session. Toggle per session with /adhd-review-mode.
plugins.oneLiner: ADHD-friendly per-reply shaping merged with Review-Ready blocker/FYI handoff summaries. Shapes the human-facing thread only — subagent returns stay full-detail.

skills.name: adhd-review-mode
skills.description: Use to toggle the adhd-review reply style for the current session.

config.name: CLAUDE_ADHD_REVIEW
config.description: Per-session kill switch. On by default — installing the plugin auto-applies the style to every new main session. Set to `0` to disable it for that session; unset (or `1`) re-enables. The style targets the main thread only; subagents never inherit it.

remove the `outputStyle` check and the frontmatter strip from `scripts/session-start.sh`. With one delivery path, the rules cannot load twice.

set `keep-coding-instructions: true` on the output style. Without it, Claude Code removes its built-in software engineering instructions while the style is active.

plugins.name: receipts
plugins.summary: A Stop hook that enforces provable claims. When the finished turn asserts a **FACT:** or a completion ('verified', 'tests pass', 'fixed', 'done'), a free deterministic prefilter checks it against that turn's real tool calls; only genuinely ambiguous claims escalate to a fresh-context Haiku judge. Unbacked claims are flagged with a ⚠ note (default `warn` mode) — or hard-gate the turn in `block` mode, where Claude must prove each with a real tool call or downgrade it to **ASSUME:** — bounded to one challenge per claim per session (ledger + stop_hook_active backstop). Enforces the fact-assume discipline (FACT = provable if challenged) that RLHF's confident 'done' quietly erodes. On by default and fail-open; set CLAUDE_RECEIPTS=0 to disable. /receipts prints the session's audit ledger and sets the mode.
plugins.oneLiner: Stop-hook claim auditor — every **FACT:** / 'verified' / 'tests pass' claim must trace to a real tool call in the transcript, or Claude is flagged (or blocked, in block mode) until it proves the claim or downgrades it to **ASSUME:**. Hybrid deterministic prefilter + fresh-context Haiku judge. On by default (mode: warn), fail-open.

commands.name: /receipts:receipts
commands.description: Show this session's receipts audit ledger, or set the audit mode: /receipts [block|warn|report|default].

config.name: CLAUDE_RECEIPTS
config.description: Master switch. On by default — installing the plugin activates the auditor. Set to `0` to disable it for a session (`1` also works, redundantly).

config.name: CLAUDE_RECEIPTS_MODE
config.description: `warn` (default) = allow the turn but inject a ⚠ note listing unbacked claims; `block` = hard-gate them until proven/downgraded; `report` = silent audit log only. Change per session with `/receipts block|warn|report` (persists until `/receipts default`); the /receipts override file takes precedence over this env var.

config.name: CLAUDE_RECEIPTS_MODEL
config.description: Model for the fresh-context judge that resolves the ambiguous claims the deterministic prefilter can't settle.

changes.text: baseline (provisional labels, structural non-claims only) on the labeled set: precision 0.000, recall 0.000, escalation_rate 0.406, dropped_at_extraction 64
audit the final assistant message, not every line of the turn. Table rows, headings, and `**ASSUME:**` lines are no longer claims.
a claim is backed only when a tool's OUTPUT shows it. A file name in a tool input no longer counts.
every verdict carries evidence, and the ledger is JSONL.
`unproven` records a claim the judge could not reach, which used to be logged as `backed`.

run the Haiku judge from a neutral folder with `--safe-mode` and no tools. A judge call no longer loads plugins, hooks, skills, agents, MCP servers, or CLAUDE.md. A test call used about 3,600 input tokens, down from about 44,000 in 0.2.1.
rewrite prose in `commands/receipts.md` and this changelog to clear the simple-english linter. No content or meaning changed, only sentence shape.
default-on with per-session opt-out
initial release, a claim-verification Stop hook
tuned prefilter (autoresearch iterations: 75→100 score)

plugins.name: obsidian-kit
plugins.tagline: One plugin for the vault: draw, format, tag
plugins.summary: create-excali and update-excali build Excalidraw drawings through ExcalidrawAutomate, lint the geometry, and review the real PNG render. format-note writes and checks notes by their note-type (map, concept, takeaway, literature, fleeting) and keeps the ASCII-diagram and callout rules of the old visualize skill. migrate-notes sets note-type across a vault and renames map notes, as one approved plan. audit-tags finds false, duplicate, typo, and off-taxonomy tags and applies one approved rename plan with backups. handover-new, handover-wrap-up, handover-init-org, and handover-init-service create and wrap up handover documents backed by the vault. session-wrap-up, session-pick-up, and session-recommend turn a working session into reflection take-aways and, after one approval, Zettelkasten cards in the vault. A dedicated skill writes and checks controlled Traditional Chinese inside the vault. A SessionStart hook primes Claude to treat the obsidian CLI as the source of truth. Vault opinions live in the vault file .obsidian-kit.json. No cross-plugin deps.
plugins.oneLiner: Work in an Obsidian vault with Claude Code: Excalidraw drawings in a house style, fixed note formats by note-type, a tag audit with one approved plan, and an obsidian CLI primer.

commands.name: /obsidian-kit:handover-init-org

commands.description: Create a well-formed handover document under ./handover/ (= LifeOS via symlink) seeded from the current conversation context.

commands.name: /obsidian-kit:handover-wrap-up
commands.description: Vault-wide daily wrap-up. Discovers active handovers, batches user decisions, executes archives/updates/suspensions in parallel. Replaces /op:wrap-up-today.

skills.name: audit-tags
skills.description: Audit the vault's tags against the approved taxonomy and apply one approved refactor plan.

skills.name: create-excali
skills.description: Create a new Obsidian Excalidraw drawing in the vault house style.

skills.name: format-note
skills.description: Write or check Obsidian notes by note-type (map, concept, takeaway, literature, fleeting).

skills.name: migrate-notes

skills.name: obsidian-bases
skills.description: Create and edit Obsidian Bases (.base files) with views, filters, formulas, and summaries.

skills.name: obsidian-markdown
skills.description: Create and edit Obsidian Flavored Markdown with wikilinks, embeds, callouts, properties, and other Obsidian-specific syntax.

skills.name: session-pick-up
skills.description: Use after wrap-up to turn chosen topic numbers into atomic Zettelkasten cards grounded in the session case and up to 3 web sources.

skills.name: session-recommend

skills.name: session-wrap-up
skills.description: Use at the end of a working or debugging session to reflect on pitfalls worth noticing and list candidate take-away topics to keep.

skills.name: update-excali
skills.description: Refine an existing Obsidian Excalidraw drawing into the vault house style.
